newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Ssangyong union declares wage freeze.
newsitem.headline: Ssangyong union declares wage freeze.

text.p: Union workers at Ssangyong Motor Co, a unit of South Korea's Ssangyong Group, would accept a wage freeze and halt all negotiation on working conditions due to rising losses, the company said on Friday.
"The labour union agreed to a wage freeze until we can turn a profit," a Ssangyong spokesman said.
Domestic media said speculation that Samsung Group was trying to take over the loss-making Ssangyong also created a sense of crisis among union workers.
Ssangyong has denied the speculation, but the trade ministry confirmed last week the two companies were in negotiations.

Ssangyong Motor is expected to post a net loss of between 150-170 billion won for 1996 on sales of 1.38 trillion won, compared with a 126.2 billion won loss on 986.74 billion revenue in 1995, the company earlier said.
In 1994, the company incurred a loss of 79.32 billion won.
The company said heavy investment in facilities in the past was the main cause for the losses.
